strings.DerivedData, old device support files an: DerivedData, old device support files and simulator caches. Xcode recreates them; the next build is slower.
strings.Download caches of npm, Gradle, node-gyp: Download caches of npm, Gradle, node-gyp, Android tools and others. They are downloaded again on demand.
strings..dmg, .pkg and .zip files in Downloads o: .dmg, .pkg and .zip files in Downloads older than 30 days. Review each one.

strings.Logs in /Library/Logs and rotated archiv: Logs in /Library/Logs and rotated archives in /private/var/log. Needs your administrator password.

strings.Clears cached network name lookups. Help: Clears cached network name lookups. Helps with slow or wrong website resolution.
strings.Asks macOS to release disk cache held in: Asks macOS to release disk cache held in memory. The effect is temporary.
strings.Clears thumbnail and preview caches. The: Clears thumbnail and preview caches. They are rebuilt as you browse files.
strings.Erases and rebuilds the search index of: Erases and rebuilds the search index of the startup disk. Fixes slow or incomplete search; indexing runs in the background for a while afterwards.
strings.The core of macOS. Manages memory, the p: The core of macOS. Manages memory, the processor and hardware; it also takes processor time on purpose to keep the Mac cool.
strings.Draws everything on screen: windows, men: Draws everything on screen: windows, menus, the Dock and animations.
strings.Starts and supervises all other processe: Starts and supervises all other processes and background services.
strings.Handles logging in and out and keeps you: Handles logging in and out and keeps your session running.
strings.The Finder: desktop, file windows and th: The Finder: desktop, file windows and the Trash.
strings.The Dock, Launchpad, Mission Control and: The Dock, Launchpad, Mission Control and the desktop background.
The right side of the menu bar.

strings.Spotlight: stores and updates the search: Spotlight: stores and updates the search index. Busy after many file changes.
strings.Spotlight: reads files so they can be fo: Spotlight: reads files so they can be found in search.
strings.Spotlight: indexes content that apps pro: Spotlight: indexes content that apps provide (mail, messages, notes).
iCloud: syncs data between your devices.

Checks for and downloads macOS updates.

strings.Graphics for web pages in Safari and oth: Graphics for web pages in Safari and other apps.
strings.Network traffic for web pages in Safari: Network traffic for web pages in Safari and other apps.
strings.A background program installed by anothe: A background program installed by another app or tool.
strings.System Events reads your login items. Fi: System Events reads your login items. Finder moves protected files to the Trash and empties the Trash. macOS can only revoke the two together; to switch off one, use System Settings.
strings.Needed for the “Old installers in Downlo: Needed for the “Old installers in Downloads” category. macOS does not let apps read this state without asking.
strings.Lets the scan see more folders. It is gi: Lets the scan see more folders. It is given and taken back only in System Settings.
strings.Desktop Peeler finds caches, logs, tempo: Desktop Peeler finds caches, logs, temporary files and leftovers, shows you exactly what it found, and removes only what you approve.
strings.Clean up your Mac. Nothing happens witho: Clean up your Mac. Nothing happens without your approval.
strings.Desktop Peeler first looks, then shows y: Desktop Peeler first looks, then shows you a list and waits. Nothing is changed until you approve that list.
strings.Desktop Peeler helps you remove files yo: Desktop Peeler helps you remove files your Mac no longer needs and shows you what starts automatically. It works in two steps everywhere: first it looks, then it shows you a list and waits. Nothing is changed until you approve that list.
strings.For the first cleanup: quit your other a: For the first cleanup: quit your other apps, open Cleanup, press Scan, open the categories to see what was found, press Review & clean…, read the list, then confirm.
strings.Scan looks for caches, logs, temporary f: Scan looks for caches, logs, temporary files and similar data and groups them into categories. Three low-risk categories are ticked for you; the others are left for you to decide. Click the arrow on a category to see every item, and the magnifying glass to see an item in Finder.
strings.Review & clean… shows every selected ite: Review & clean… shows every selected item with its size and location. Confirm to go ahead, or Cancel to change nothing. Categories marked “admin password” contain files shared by all users; Finder will ask for your password for those.
strings.Empty Trash afterwards is ticked by defa: Empty Trash afterwards is ticked by default: after the items are moved to the Trash, the whole Trash is emptied, including anything that was already in it. Emptying is permanent. Untick it if you want to be able to put items back.
strings.After cleaning, apps recreate their cach: After cleaning, apps recreate their caches as they need them, so some apps open a little slower the first time and part of the space is used again over time.
strings.This pane lists programs that start by t: This pane lists programs that start by themselves when you log in or when the Mac starts. Tick the ones you want to stop and press Remove selected from auto-start…. The programs stay installed; they simply no longer start automatically. The change applies from your next login or restart.
strings.A “program missing” badge means the entr: A “program missing” badge means the entry points to a program that no longer exists; such entries are safe candidates for removal.
strings.Some apps register background items dire: Some apps register background items directly with macOS. Those can only be switched off in System Settings › General › Login Items; use the button at the bottom to go there.
strings.Run checks looks for startup entries who: Run checks looks for startup entries whose program is gone, shortcuts (symbolic links) that point nowhere, and settings files of apps that seem to be uninstalled. It also shows the health and free space of your startup disk. Nothing is ticked for you; Select all ticks every finding at once.
strings.The settings-file list is an estimate. I: The settings-file list is an estimate. If you recognize an app you still use, leave its file alone. Removing a settings file resets that app's preferences.
strings.Verify disk structure checks the startup: Verify disk structure checks the startup disk without changing it. If it reports problems, repair the disk with Apple's Disk Utility (First Aid).
strings.Each action solves a specific problem; n: Each action solves a specific problem; none of them is needed regularly. Run… shows the exact command before anything happens.
strings.Flush DNS cache helps when websites do n: Flush DNS cache helps when websites do not open or open the wrong address. Free inactive memory releases memory macOS uses as cache; the effect is short-lived. Reset Quick Look cache fixes wrong or missing file previews. Rebuild Spotlight index fixes search that misses files; searching is incomplete until indexing finishes, which can take a while.
strings.The process list shows what is using the: The process list shows what is using the most memory right now. Point at a process to see what it does. To close a program, quit it normally or use Activity Monitor.
strings.A record of everything Desktop Peeler ch: A record of everything Desktop Peeler changed since you opened it. It is cleared when you quit the app.
strings.Theme: Same as macOS, Dark or Light. The: Theme: Same as macOS, Dark or Light. The switch in the top bar changes the same setting.
strings.Language: “Same as macOS” uses the Mac's: Language: “Same as macOS” uses the Mac's language if a translation exists, otherwise English.
strings.Remembered approvals: if you tick “Don't: Remembered approvals: if you tick “Don't ask again” on an approval sheet, that kind of action runs without waiting for your approval from then on. The result is still shown and logged. Each one can be revoked in Settings.
strings.macOS permissions: shows what macOS allo: macOS permissions: shows what macOS allows Desktop Peeler to do, and lets you revoke each permission. macOS asks again the next time it is needed.
strings.Each language is one file. In Settings ›: Each language is one file. In Settings › Language press Save English template…, open the file in a text editor, set “code” (for example “de”) and “name” (for example “Deutsch”), and translate every value on the right-hand side under “strings”. Leave the left-hand side and placeholders such as %d and %@ unchanged.
strings.Then press Add language file… and choose: Then press Add language file… and choose the file. Texts that are missing stay in English. A file with the same code as a built-in language replaces it.
strings.Only if Empty Trash afterwards was not t: Only if Empty Trash afterwards was not ticked: open the Trash, select the items and choose Put Back. Emptied items cannot be put back.
strings.Why did the free space not change?: Why did the free space not change?
strings.Files in the Trash still take space. Emp: Files in the Trash still take space. Empty the Trash, or leave Empty Trash afterwards ticked.
strings.Why does macOS ask whether Desktop Peele: Why does macOS ask whether Desktop Peeler may control Finder or System Events?
strings.System Events is used to read your login: System Events is used to read your login items. Finder is used to move protected files to the Trash and to empty the Trash. Desktop Peeler uses them for nothing else.
strings.Why am I asked for my password?: Why am I asked for my password?
strings.Some files and commands belong to the sy: Some files and commands belong to the system. macOS asks for the password; Desktop Peeler never sees or stores it.
strings.Some items “could not be removed”. Is th: Some items “could not be removed”. Is that a problem?
strings.No. macOS protects some files. They were: No. macOS protects some files. They were left exactly as they were.
strings.Is it safe to delete caches?: Is it safe to delete caches?
strings.Caches are copies that apps can recreate: Caches are copies that apps can recreate. Quit the app first; an app that is running may misbehave until restarted.
strings.Does Desktop Peeler run in the backgroun: Does Desktop Peeler run in the background or send data anywhere?
strings.No. It works only while it is open, and: No. It works only while it is open, and it does not connect to the internet.
strings.Should I give it Full Disk Access?: Should I give it Full Disk Access?
strings.Optional. With it the scan sees more fol: Optional. With it the scan sees more folders. Without it the app still works.
strings.This is not a Desktop Peeler language fi: This is not a Desktop Peeler language file. It needs “code”, “name” and “strings” entries.
strings.Theme, language, remembered approvals an: Theme, language, remembered approvals and the macOS permissions Desktop Peeler uses.
strings.“Same as macOS” follows the light or dar: “Same as macOS” follows the light or dark appearance set in System Settings.
strings.“Same as macOS” uses the Mac's language: “Same as macOS” uses the Mac's language if a translation exists, otherwise English. Each language is one file; you can add new ones.
strings.A language file with every text in Engli: A language file with every text in English. Translate it and add it with “Add language file…”. See Help › Adding a language.
strings.Actions you allowed with “Don't ask agai: Actions you allowed with “Don't ask again”. They run without waiting for your approval; the result is still shown and logged. Revoke one to be asked again.
strings.None. Every change asks for your approva: None. Every change asks for your approval.
What macOS allows Desktop Peeler to do. After revoking, macOS asks again the next time the permission is needed.
strings.Administrator password: macOS asks for i: Administrator password: macOS asks for it each time it is needed. Desktop Peeler never sees or stores it, so there is nothing to revoke.
strings.Nothing is changed without your approval: Nothing is changed without your approval. Removed files go to the Trash.
strings.Don't ask again for this kind of action: Don't ask again for this kind of action (revocable in Settings)
strings.Working… If macOS or Finder asks for you: Working… If macOS or Finder asks for your password, the request may be behind this window.
strings.Approved automatically: you chose “Don't: Approved automatically: you chose “Don't ask again” for this action. You can revoke it in Settings.
strings.Scan first, tick what may go, then revie: Scan first, tick what may go, then review the full list before anything is moved to the Trash.
strings.Press Scan to look for caches, logs, tem: Press Scan to look for caches, logs, temporary files and other removable data. Scanning changes nothing.
strings.After the items are moved, the whole Tra: After the items are moved, the whole Trash is emptied. This is permanent.
strings.Programs that start by themselves at log: Programs that start by themselves at login or boot. Tick the ones you want to stop from auto-starting.
strings.Press Load list. macOS may ask once whet: Press Load list. macOS may ask once whether Desktop Peeler may control “System Events”; this is needed to read your login items.
strings.Open Login Items in System Settings: Open Login Items in System Settings
strings.Background items that apps register with: Background items that apps register with macOS directly can only be switched off there.
strings.Checking changes nothing, and nothing is: Checking changes nothing, and nothing is preselected.
strings.Runs “diskutil verifyVolume /”. The Mac: Runs “diskutil verifyVolume /”. The Mac can feel slow while it runs. Repairs, if needed, are done with Disk Utility.
strings.Each action shows the exact command and: Each action shows the exact command and asks for confirmation before it runs.
strings.Everything Desktop Peeler changed since: Everything Desktop Peeler changed since it was opened.
